import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch.  Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# ChangeSpec name -> branch name conversion.
is_changespec = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_changespec:
        # ChangeSpec ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

marker.step_source:
head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_file=$(mktemp /tmp/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff)
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

## What I did — sase-93.1

**Problem:** `sase init repo --check` is a read-only planning command, but it raised a hard blocker whenever the machine-level `agents` sidecar couldn't resolve an owning SASE project key — which is exactly the CI situation, since the checkout isn't under a registered project.

**Fix:**
- `src/sase/sdd/_sidecar_init.py` — split out `resolve_sidecar_clone_root()`, which returns `None` *only* for the unresolvable-project-key case, plus `unresolved_project_key_message()`. `sidecar_clone_root()` is now a thin wrapper that still raises, so the mutating paths (`initialize_sidecars`, `initialize_materialized_sidecars`, `run_materialized_sidecars`) are behaviorally unchanged.
- `src/sase/main/_repo_init_sidecars.py` — `plan_sidecar_actions()` returns `(actions, warnings)` and skips unresolvable specs with a warning instead of raising.
- `src/sase/main/repo_init_handler.py` — threads those warnings into the plan; the `except SddMaterializationError` blocker path still covers every other sidecar planning failure.
- `tests/main/test_repo_init_plan.py` — a test asserting the plan has no blockers, no `agents` actions, and a warning; plus one asserting the mutating entry point still raises.

**Verification:** `just check` passes fully (fmt, ruff, mypy, keep-sorted, symvision, toobig, SASE validation, tests).

Two things worth flagging that cost time and are unrelated to the change:
- `/tmp` (a 32G tmpfs) filled up mid-run and blocked all shell access; the culprit was multi-GB pytest logs I'd redirected there. Cleared.
- Two earlier full-suite runs had unrelated flaky failures under machine load (12 `tests/llm_provider/` alias tests once, `test_residual_freeze_soak` once — the latter also fails on a clean `HEAD`). Both pass in isolation and the final clean `just check` was green.

Bead `sase-93.1` is closed; the parent epic `sase-93` was left open. One non-fatal warning from the commit: agent-hood publication for `kc` was deferred and will retry on its own.
